---
title: "How do I test and interpret linear association between two measurements?"
---

## Question

How do I test and interpret linear association between two measurements?

## Decide which method fits

Check paired measurements; draw a scatterplot for nonlinearity and influential points; calculate Pearson r with an interval and test under explicit assumptions.

## Worked example: cars

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("cars")
fit <- ru_apply("correlation_test", d, x="speed", y="dist", confidence=.95)
stopifnot(is.finite(fit$estimate))
```

The fitted coefficient measures linear association between speed and stopping distance in recorded cars. It is not a causal-effect estimate and can be distorted by unusual observations or a curved relationship.

## Apply to another dataset

```r
ru_apply("correlation_test", your_data, x="first_numeric_column", y="second_numeric_column", confidence=.95)
```

If the question is about ranks or a monotonic relationship, inspect whether spearman_correlation better matches the task.

## Optional Palmer penguins example

```r
if (requireNamespace("palmerpenguins", quietly=TRUE)) {
  d <- ru_data("penguins")
  ru_apply("correlation_test", d, x="bill_length_mm", y="body_mass_g", confidence=.95)
}
```

Review assumptions and available input conditions with `ru_plan("correlation_test")`. A valid computation does not itself verify the underlying study design.
